\chapter{Six Small Form Labels}
\label{ch:mr-a1-form-labels}
\hlchaptermodality{19}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read, copy, and retrieve six Marathi form labels, while keeping the two favorite-label agreement endings distinct.}

After a delay and without a visible answer model, write the final three form labels and repair agreement before other spelling.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[nāv: Mīrā]{\mr{नाव} — the first form label}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-naav}



\begin{quote}
You already know \textbf{\mr{नाव}} as “name.” On a form, the same word becomes a request: write the name after it. Today the answer is the familiar practice name \textbf{\mr{मीरा}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace only \textbf{\mr{नाव}: \mr{मीरा}}. Keep the colon between the printed label and the answer. Then cover the line and point to the part that asks the question.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one label and one known answer.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[śahar: Puṇe]{\mr{शहर} — the city box}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-shahar}



\begin{quote}
The known sentence \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{पुण्यात} \mr{राहतो} / \mr{राहते}} put the practice person in Pune. A short form asks for that place with \textbf{\mr{शहर}} — “city.”
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace only \textbf{\mr{शहर}: \mr{पुणे}}. Say “city, Pune” once. Do not add an address; this box asks for one small thing.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Two labels are enough for one sitting.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhāṣā: marāṭhī]{\mr{भाषा} — the language box}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-bhasha}



\begin{quote}
You can already say \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{मराठी} \mr{बोलतो} / \mr{बोलते}}. A form compresses that whole sentence to a label and a value: \textbf{\mr{भाषा}: \mr{मराठी}} — “language: Marathi.”
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace \textbf{\mr{भाषा}: \mr{मराठी}} once. Keep \textbf{\mr{भाषा}} on the question side and \textbf{\mr{मराठी}} on the answer side.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop before the form grows longer.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āvaḍte pey: chahā]{\mr{आवडते} \mr{पेय} — favorite drink}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-avdate-pey}



\begin{quote}
The known drink is \textbf{\mr{चहा}}. The label \textbf{\mr{आवडते} \mr{पेय}} means “favorite drink.” \textbf{\mr{पेय}} is neuter, so the describing word takes neuter \textbf{-\mr{ते}}: \textbf{\mr{आवडते}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace \textbf{\mr{आवडते} \mr{पेय}: \mr{चहा}} once. Box only the ending \textbf{-\mr{ते}}. The next lesson will change that ending for a feminine label; do not learn both today.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One agreement ending is enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āvaḍtī kṛtī: vācaṇe]{\mr{आवडती} \mr{कृती} — favorite activity}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-avadti-kruti}



\begin{quote}
Change one thing. \textbf{\mr{कृती}}, “activity,” is feminine, so “favorite” becomes feminine \textbf{\mr{आवडती}}. The familiar activity value is \textbf{\mr{वाचणे}}, “reading.”
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace \textbf{\mr{आवडती} \mr{कृती}: \mr{वाचणे}} once. Underline only \textbf{-\mr{ती}}. Compare without rewriting: \textbf{\mr{आवडते} \mr{पेय}} but \textbf{\mr{आवडती} \mr{कृती}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after the one-ending contrast.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mitrāce nāv: Aruṇ]{\mr{मित्राचे} \mr{नाव} — friend's name}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F01-mitrache-naav}



\begin{quote}
You know \textbf{\mr{मित्र}}, friend, and \textbf{\mr{नाव}}, name. Marathi links them as \textbf{\mr{मित्राचे} \mr{नाव}}, “the friend's name.” The \textbf{-\mr{चे}} form agrees with neuter \textbf{\mr{नाव}}. The familiar practice answer is \textbf{\mr{अरुण}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one pair}
Trace \textbf{\mr{मित्राचे} \mr{नाव}: \mr{अरुण}} once. Circle \textbf{-\mr{चे}} and stop; no possessive table is needed for this form.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
All six labels now have one first encounter.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nāv · śahar · bhāṣā]{Copy the first three rows}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F02-first-three-copy}



\begin{quote}
Say the three meanings once: name, city, language. Keep the model closed until you can say all three in that order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — guided copy}
Copy exactly three short rows:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{नाव}: \mr{मीरा}}
\end{quote}

>

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{शहर}: \mr{पुणे}} \textbf{\mr{भाषा}: \mr{मराठी}}
\end{quote}

After each row, point left of the colon and say what that label asks. Repair only a missing or misplaced character; do not add a fourth row.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Close the model before the next lesson.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āvaḍte pey · āvaḍtī kṛtī · mitrāce nāv]{Copy the last three rows}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F02-last-three-copy}



\begin{quote}
Say the three meanings once: favorite drink, favorite activity, friend's name. Listen for the one small job each label performs.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — guided copy}
Copy exactly three rows:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{आवडते} \mr{पेय}: \mr{चहा}}
\end{quote}

>

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{आवडती} \mr{कृती}: \mr{वाचणे}} \textbf{\mr{मित्राचे} \mr{नाव}: \mr{अरुण}}
\end{quote}

On the first two, underline only \textbf{-\mr{ते} / -\mr{ती}}. On the third, circle only \textbf{-\mr{चे}}. One visible contrast, then stop.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Close the model before retrieval.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nāv · śahar · bhāṣā]{Hide, wait, write the first three labels}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F03-first-three-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Close the copy lesson. Say name, city, language once, then start the ten-second delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Close the copy lesson and wait ten seconds. From the meaning cues \textbf{name · city · language}, write the three Marathi labels. There is no Devanagari model and no romanization in this attempt.

Only after all three are written, reopen the model. Check one row at a time and repair only the first differing character.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one delayed set.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āvaḍte pey · āvaḍtī kṛtī · mitrāce nāv]{Hide, wait, write the last three labels}

\label{lesson:MR-A1F03-last-three-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Close the copy lesson. Say favorite drink, favorite activity, friend's name once, then start the ten-second delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Close the copy lesson and wait ten seconds. From \textbf{favorite drink · favorite activity · friend's name}, write the three Marathi labels without a model or romanization.

Then compare in two bounded passes: first \textbf{-\mr{ते} / -\mr{ती}}, then \textbf{-\mr{चे}}. If the first pass differs, repair it and stop; leave the second pass for tomorrow.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The labels are ready; choosing answers belongs to the next runway.
\end{tcolorbox}
